title: Getting the tenor saxophone chair in the school stage band
summary: When the stage band's tenor player falls ill, Cobb is pulled out of Latin class to rehearse and takes over the tenor, which he has played ever since.

bands.name: Phillis Wheatley High School stage band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Finally, one day in Phyllis Wheatley High School where I attended and graduated in 1935, my first class to me was rotten and I had a teacher that was so firm -- she was a Christian Scientist. She didn't believe in you getting sick or nothing. And the tenor saxophone player took sick and we were playing -- the band was playing at the Ethiopian Cafe on Mylom (phonetic) and I wanted to be in that band so bad I didn't know what to do. He took sick, God bless him.
Phyllis Wheatly High School stage band.
But I wasn't playing in it. I had C melody and it didn't fit.
I see. How big was this stage band?
Yeah, well, I mean it was a band out of the sort of marching band.
No, no, no, I'm not talking about the marching band. I'm talking about the stage band that's playing
music for dinner music and this sort of thing.

All right. I'm in the first class which Agry COLA, which is a fan MR. PUELLA, PUELLA, I don't like (unintelligible) girl and boy, Latin. What the hell I need with Latin? What -- I'm not going to be a doctor. And she's -- that's my first period class. And I'm not lying to you. And they sent a message in there, please release Arnett Cobb to come down and rehearse with the stage band. And she said, Arnett Cobb, you are excused to go down to the auditorium for rehearsal with the band. I said, 'Thank you,' and they put me on tenor saxophone. No more C melody. That's how I got the tenor. And the young man that took sick could never play no more. The doctor told him he couldn't play anymore and I fell heir to the horn. That's how I happen to play tenor today.
